body.html: The Impress Sisaket Hotel is a small city hotel in central Sisaket, on Srisumang Road in the Mueang Tai subdistrict of Mueang Sisaket District · It opened in 2014 and has around 28 rooms · It's a simple, no-frills place that doesn't aim for luxury design but focuses on being clean, quiet and affordable · Several reviews describe it as a family-run hotel where the owner is hands-on, giving it a level of care you don't always get from larger chains.

Most rooms are Classic doubles or twins of around 28 square metres · What guests consistently praise is that the rooms are clean, the bedding and towels have no musty smell, the air conditioning is cold and the bathroom water is fine · Every room has air conditioning, a refrigerator, a flat-screen TV and Wi-Fi that several reviews call genuinely fast · The in-room kit is complete for the price — not luxurious, but a good fit for what you pay, ideal for travellers who want a clean room to rest in rather than full resort facilities.
"Clean room, towels and blankets with no musty smell, the owner and staff are very friendly, free breakfast and free parking · quiet and good for resting — great value at a few hundred baht."

What sets it apart from similarly priced places is that it includes free breakfast and has an on-site restaurant · Breakfast is simple — toast, rice soup/congee and coffee, served roughly 7:30–10:00 AM · It's not a big buffet, but at this price it's an advantage · There's free on-site parking, laundry service and bicycles to rent for getting around town · Pet owners also like that cats stay free, which is rare in a small-town hotel.

It sits in the Mueang Tai area of central Sisaket, about 500 metres from Wat Chiang Ei and within walking distance of Sanam Luang Park · Wat Maha Phuttharam (Wat Phra To) and the Sisaket Aquarium are around 2–2.5 km away, a few minutes by car · Sisaket Train Station is roughly 2.5 km away · One thing many reviews note is that the hotel is set deep down a soi and can be tricky to find the first time — having navigation open helps a lot.

To be straight with you, per real guest reviews: the limitations mentioned are that there's no lift and no swimming pool, and as a small property the facilities are basic · Some reviews mention inconsistent housekeeping, with dust in a few rooms · A few guests feel the staff keep too close an eye on comings and goings · And because it's away from the busy shopping streets, the surroundings are quiet at night — great for resting, but you may need to drive out for late-night food.

In short: if you want somewhere quiet and clean in central Sisaket with free breakfast and free parking, at a few hundred baht, and you don't mind the lack of a lift or pool — The Impress Sisaket Hotel is a fitting choice · The 7.3 from 39 Trip.com reviews captures it well: a small, quiet, good-value hotel that suits self-drivers, one-night stopovers on a southern-Isan trip, or anyone travelling with a pet.

A tip from following the reviews here: open your navigation before you arrive, as the hotel is deep down a soi with no prominent sign · And if you're here for a quiet break, rent one of the hotel bikes and ride to Wat Chiang Ei and Sanam Luang Park in the morning — an easy activity that fits the town's relaxed mood.

faq.q: Where is The Impress Sisaket Hotel, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The Impress Sisaket Hotel is at 1542/54 Srisumang Road, Mueang Tai subdistrict, in central Sisaket · It's about 500 m from Wat Chiang Ei and within walking distance of Sanam Luang Park · Wat Maha Phuttharam (Wat Phra To), the Sisaket Aquarium and the train station are around 2–2.5 km away, a few minutes by car · The hotel sits deep down a soi, so navigation is recommended.

faq.q: How much does The Impress Sisaket Hotel cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿450/night for a Classic Double with a king bed · Twin and Superior rooms run about ฿490–฿550 · There are also monthly rooms from around ฿3,500–4,500/month for long stays · Prices vary by season, so compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does The Impress Sisaket Hotel have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: Yes to both · There's free simple breakfast (toast, congee, coffee) served roughly 7:30–10:00 AM, and free on-site parking · It also has an on-site restaurant, laundry service and bikes to rent — handy for self-drivers.

faq.q: Does The Impress Sisaket Hotel have a lift and a pool?
faq.a: Neither a lift nor a swimming pool · It's a small 28-room hotel with basic facilities, focused on cleanliness and quiet rather than amenities · For a pool and full facilities, look at a larger city hotel.

faq.q: Is The Impress Sisaket Hotel pet-friendly?
faq.a: Yes · Cats stay free here, which is rare for a small-town hotel · It's best to let the hotel know in advance when booking so they can prepare a suitable room.

faq.q: Who is The Impress Sisaket Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers who want a small, quiet, clean place in central Sisaket with free breakfast and free parking, at a few hundred baht · It suits self-drivers, one-night stopovers on a southern-Isan trip, and pet owners · It's less suited to those who need a lift, a pool, or the full facilities of a larger hotel.
